name: Facet
text: Make the graph’s nodes shrink slightly when idle, then return to normal size. This draws attention to the graph’s activity without overwhelming the user, balancing visibility and calm. The trade-off is reduced precision in node size for better perceived liveliness.

name: Pane
text: The shrinking nodes risk training users to ignore the signal entirely—like a car alarm that blares until ignored. A better alternative: pulse the node border color once when idle, then fade back to normal. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure how often users notice changes in each version.

name: Facet
text:
Make the graph’s edges pulse once with a bright highlight when new data arrives. This signals freshness without clutter—users see the change instantly, then the graph settles. The trade-off is a brief visual burst that could distract if overused, but it’s faster and clearer than shrinking nodes. Test it against the border pulse to confirm which users notice faster.

name: Pane
text: Edge pulses risk training users to treat every highlight as noise—like a stock ticker that blinks so often it’s ignored. A better alternative: fade the edge to a subtle, persistent color shift (e.g., a soft glow) for 3 seconds after new data arrives. Settle it by tracking how many users click on edges within 5 seconds of the change—fewer clicks mean the signal is too weak.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a **subtle 3-second edge glow** (not pulse) to signal new data, paired with a **node border pulse** (not shrink) for idle attention—settle via A/B test tracking user clicks and dwell time.

Result: A graph that feels alive without training users to ignore it. Owned by Pane.
